svg.title: IronGrind Detailed System Architecture
svg.desc: Implementation-level system architecture for IronGrind, tracing sign-in and role lookup, registration and approval, QR attendance, product inventory, walk-in sales, member portal operations, report queries, Supabase JavaScript requests, row-level security, database tables, and PostgreSQL.
svg.text: IRON GRIND FITNESS GYM MEMBERSHIP & OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Detailed system architecture — browser workflows, Supabase requests, access control, and database records
Email + password submitted by either role
Validates credentials and returns user + session
Select profile by Auth user ID; route according to role
pending / rejected / not found → show status
draft recovery is browser-local until saved
Separate staff-created-member path: admin.html → functions.invoke(admin-create-member) → verify admin → Auth Admin API → service-role admin_create_member_and_sale RPC → members + sales + sale_items
Authenticated browser session → Supabase JavaScript client
Frontend JavaScript makes direct Supabase Auth / table / RPC calls; staff account creation also invokes a Supabase Edge Function

g.text: SELECT members by ID / auth ID / username
check membership expiry and open visit
date ordered and displayed in browser
price, unit, active state, stock, image
gram quantity for supplements; items for merch
function checks auth.uid() and linked member
no online purchasing or payment gateway
Supabase returns rows allowed by RLS
report calculation and display run in frontend
sale and sale-item records, as authorized

svg.text: Calls originate in frontend JavaScript using the authenticated Supabase client
RLS protects direct authenticated table calls; privileged Edge Function calls use a service role and verify the admin identity
POSTGRESQL APPLICATION TABLES AND AUTH IDENTITY LINK
query results return through the same authenticated client
Figure 3. System Architecture Diagram — actual browser-to-Supabase workflows; hosting serves static files, while Supabase provides Auth and database services.
Note: Realtime subscriptions are used for selected views only; ordinary database reads and writes do not require Realtime to be enabled.
